details:
I wanted to throw an idea out there about the current 10MB avatar upload limit for Android and Quest users. I've been thinking about this for a while, and I honestly wonder if it's something VRChat could look into again.

I completely understand why VRChat has restrictions in place. The game needs to run smoothly, people use different headsets, and not everyone has the same hardware. I'm not saying those restrictions should just disappear. But at the same time, I think it's worth asking whether the current 10MB limit is still the best option, especially when we're talking about the Quest 2 and Quest 3.

One thing that caught my attention is that the 10MB limit isn't necessarily the absolute limit of what the headset itself can handle. It's a restriction VRChat has chosen to help maintain performance and keep things running properly. Obviously, that doesn't mean the Quest 2 can suddenly handle massive avatars without problems, but it does make me curious about something: have we actually reached the point where 10MB is the most reasonable limit, or is there some room to give creators a little more freedom?

For some context, the Quest 2 uses a Snapdragon XR2 processor, an Adreno 650 GPU, and 6GB of RAM. The Quest 3 has newer hardware, so naturally, the two devices aren't going to perform exactly the same. I think that difference is worth considering instead of automatically treating every standalone headset the same way.

From what I've seen in VRChat's Android avatar documentation, the current restrictions include a 10MB compressed download size and a 40MB uncompressed size. Those are two different measurements, and I think that's important to understand. Just because an avatar takes up 10MB when downloaded doesn't necessarily mean it will only use 10MB of memory once it's loaded into VRChat.

So instead of immediately jumping to something like 50MB, what if VRChat started experimenting with smaller increases?

For example, maybe the Quest 2 could be tested with a 15MB or 20MB limit, while the Quest 3 could potentially be tested with something higher. I'm not saying those numbers are guaranteed to work. They're just examples of what could be tested to see where the actual limits are.

There are also a few things VRChat could potentially improve to make this more realistic.

1. Better avatar compression

If VRChat could improve how avatar files are compressed, creators might be able to keep more of their avatar's details without making the download size unnecessarily large. Nobody wants to spend hours creating an avatar just to remove half of its textures and details because they're over the upload limit.

2. Different limits for different headsets

This is probably one of my biggest suggestions. The Quest 2 and Quest 3 don't have identical hardware, so why should they necessarily have identical restrictions?

I understand that supporting older devices is important, especially since plenty of people are still using the Quest 2. But perhaps newer headsets could receive higher limits while older devices keep their current restrictions. That way, VRChat wouldn't have to sacrifice compatibility just to give newer hardware more room.

3. Automatic avatar optimization

Another idea would be to give creators an optional optimization tool when uploading avatars. Something that checks for unnecessarily large textures, excessive polygons, expensive materials, and other things that could affect performance.

Instead of creators having to manually search through everything and figure out what needs to be changed, VRChat could help point out the biggest problems and possibly suggest ways to fix them.

4. Better texture management

Textures are another thing worth considering. A lot of the visual quality in an avatar comes from its textures, especially when it comes to clothing, hair, accessories, and smaller details.

Maybe VRChat could look into better texture compression, resolution scaling, or other ways of managing textures. That could potentially help creators keep their avatars looking good without putting as much pressure on standalone hardware.

5. Actually testing the limits of the hardware

This is something I'd genuinely like to know more about.

Has VRChat ever tested different avatar download sizes on actual Quest 2 and Quest 3 hardware to see where performance starts becoming a serious problem?

For example, developers could compare avatars at 10MB, 15MB, 20MB, 25MB, and 30MB while monitoring FPS, RAM usage, GPU usage, loading times, and crashes.

It would also be important to test these avatars in different situations. An avatar might run perfectly fine by itself in an empty world, but that doesn't necessarily mean it will perform well in a crowded instance with several other avatars loaded at the same time.

I think testing those situations would give everyone a much better understanding of what these headsets can realistically handle.

6. Looking beyond download size alone

I think this is probably one of the most important parts of the discussion.

A compressed avatar download size doesn't tell the entire story about how demanding that avatar will be once it's running in VRChat. There are other things to consider, including textures, materials, polygons, memory usage, and overall performance.

VRChat already has avatar performance rankings that help identify avatars that might be demanding on a device. Maybe those systems could work alongside more flexible upload limits instead of relying so heavily on one compressed file-size restriction.

I'm not saying file size doesn't matter. It absolutely does. I just think there could be a better way to balance it with everything else that affects performance.

My biggest question is:

Has VRChat ever looked into the actual maximum compressed avatar size that the Quest 2 and Quest 3 could realistically support through internal hardware testing?

I'm not asking for every Quest user to suddenly download 30MB or 50MB avatars. I understand that would create problems if it wasn't handled properly.

What I'm really suggesting is that VRChat could investigate whether the current 10MB limit is still necessary at its current level, especially as newer standalone headsets become available.

The Quest 2 is still being used by plenty of VRChat players, and the Quest 3 offers newer hardware with additional capabilities. I don't think supporting older hardware and improving the experience for newer hardware have to be mutually exclusive.

At the end of the day, I just think creators could benefit from having a little more room to work with. More room for detailed clothing, better textures, hairstyles, accessories, and other visual features without constantly having to remove things just to get under the upload limit.

I understand that performance has to come first, and I wouldn't want a change that makes VRChat worse for everyone else. But I also don't think we should automatically assume that 10MB is the best possible limit without continuing to evaluate what the hardware can handle.

This is just an idea I've been thinking about, and I'm genuinely interested in hearing what the development team thinks. Even if increasing the limit isn't currently possible, I'd like to know whether this is something VRChat has tested or considered for the future.

Maybe there's a reasonable middle ground that gives creators more freedom while still keeping Quest users' performance in mind.

Here are the main points I was suggesting:

Increase the current 10MB Android avatar upload limit through gradual testing.

Consider different upload limits for Quest 2, Quest 3, and newer standalone headsets.

Improve avatar compression so creators can maintain visual quality while reducing file sizes.

Introduce optional automatic avatar optimization to help creators identify performance issues.

Improve texture compression, resolution scaling, and memory management.

Test different avatar sizes (15MB, 20MB, 25MB, and 30MB) on actual Quest hardware.

Monitor FPS, RAM usage, GPU usage, loading times, and crashes during testing.

Consider using avatar performance rankings alongside more flexible upload limits.

My main point is that I don't think VRChat should blindly increase the limit. I think the team should investigate what the hardware can realistically handle and whether the current 10MB restriction could be improved without hurting performance.
title: Brainstorm: Could VRChat reconsider the 10MB Android avatar upload limit?
